An International Innovation Hub for Songdo

A unified proposal to activate IGC's international assets and establish a global startup ecosystem in Songdo.

Songdo's Advantages

Why Songdo Stands Out

Korea's only international campus, a premier biopharmaceutical cluster driven by industry giants like Samsung, Celltrion, SK, and Lotte Biologics, and a vast concentration of international organizations—including the Green Climate Fund (GCF), World Bank, GGGI, and 15 UN agencies (ESCAP, APCICT, UNDRR, OSD, etc.)—are all integrated within a single metropolitan area.

Bio-Medicine Hub
Samsung, Celltrion, SK Bioscience, Lotte Biologics — world-class biomanufacturing capacity.
Global Organizations
GCF, World Bank, GGGI, and 15 UN agencies (ESCAP, APCICT, UNDRR, etc.) — a robust physical nexus for global governance and cooperation

IGC's Hidden Potential

Global Talent Pool

No single campus in Korea possesses a multinational talent pool of this magnitude. Korean, English, Chinese, and Southeast Asian languages coexist within a single building.

Where Our Students Come From

Songdo's Challenges

What Holds Songdo Back

Despite its biopharmaceutical assets and international organizations, Songdo's startup ecosystem is being eclipsed by Pangyo. Regional gross domestic product growth has decelerated, and Songdo's distinctive identity remains undefined.

01
Slow Startup Growth
Pangyo tenants grew (1,622 in '22 → 1,803 in '24). Songdo's Startup Park supported a cumulative 78 firms, selecting 40 with 26 collaborations in 2024.
02
Slow Local Economy
Songdo's share of Incheon's GRDP has plateaued, with new employment creation disproportionately concentrated in biomanufacturing.
03
No Clear Identity
Pangyo is synonymous with K-tech; Daejeon with R&D — Songdo has yet to establish a definitive brand narrative linking its biopharmaceutical and international assets.

IGC's Digital Gaps

Problems with the IGC Website

The Foundation, SUNY, Mason, Ghent, Utah, LMS, email, and facilities — each operates as an independent site. There is no unified search functionality, mobile responsiveness is inadequate, and external traffic has effectively ceased.

01
8+ Separate Sites
The Foundation, SUNY Korea, George Mason, Ghent, Utah, LMS, email, and facilities systems all operate independently. The user journey to access information is excessively convoluted.
02
Old / Mismatched Design
Table-based layouts, popup notices, and Flash remnants persist. The absence of cross-site design standards erodes brand credibility. Multiple sites lack responsive design.
03
Few Visitors / Low Use
No search functionality, no multilingual support, and weak mobile optimization. External traffic has effectively stalled, with no social media or search engine integration.

Empty Basement Space

Empty Basement

The majority of floor B1 remains underutilized, with no lease model established for external tenant occupancy. These constitute idle assets generating only maintenance costs.

B1: Mostly Empty
Without a tenant acquisition model, this space generates only maintenance expenditures. Vacancy directly increases the Foundation's financial burden.
Few Basement Shops
Low foot traffic precludes commercial district formation; the absence of commercial activity further discourages foot traffic — a self-reinforcing vicious cycle.

Our Solution · 01

Songdo's Problems Solved by IGC

A solution that integrates three assets unique to IGC — space, students, and internationality — into a unified framework.

01
Empty Basement → Founders Rent First
Lease underutilized basement space in IGC Center to entrepreneurs on preferential terms, lowering barriers to entry for early-stage Songdo-based startups.
02
Global Students ↔ Founders
Match IGC's multinational student body with resident founders, thereby operationalizing Songdo's claim as an "international city."
03
Students ↔ Local Businesses
Directly connect international students with Songdo-based enterprises, actively driving the internationalization of the district's industrial base.

Our Solution · 02

One Platform for All

Unify 8 disparate websites into a single Boreum Dari, redesign the interface with a contemporary UI, and implement proactive promotion strategies to increase utilization.

01
Many Sites → One Hub
Consolidate 8+ domains into a single Boreum Dari domain. Maximize usability through integrated search and a unified access pathway.
02
Old Design → Fresh Design
Apply a cohesive design system with responsive layouts and multilingual support, substantially improving accessibility and user experience.
03
More Promotion → More Use
Leverage social media integration, search engine optimization, and student-generated content to actively increase external traffic.

Our Solution · 03

From IGC Vacancy to Industry Hub

Three cascading effects generated by the strategic utilization of vacant basement space.

01
Songdo First → Bigger Market
Prioritize Songdo-based businesses with preferential lease terms, directly catalyzing the growth of Songdo's entrepreneurial market.
02
More Visitors → Busier Shops
Influx of resident enterprises and visitors organically stimulates basement commercial district formation, activating the surrounding commercial ecosystem.
03
Students Join In → Real Experience
Students participate directly in the management of resident enterprises, acquiring hands-on entrepreneurial experience and developing professionally within IGC Center.

Working Together

Three Partners, One Team

No single stakeholder can realize this vision independently. A multi-layered governance structure encompassing policy, capital, and accreditation is a fundamental precondition.

Revenue Model

Three Ways to Earn

Rather than a single income source, long-term financial self-sufficiency is achieved through three pillars: leasing, investment, and platform operations.

01
Basement Rent Income
Secure stable baseline revenue by leasing IGC Center basement space to entrepreneurs.
02
Investing in Startups → Returns
Actively invest in revenue-generating resident enterprises to acquire equity stakes and generate investment returns.
03
Platform Business
Systematize the entire operation as a unified platform, developing it into a scalable long-term business model.
